title: Discovery of furopyridine-based compounds as novel inhibitors of Janus kinase 2: In silico and in vitro studies.
authors: Suriya, Utid; Mahalapbutr, Panupong; Geronikaki, Athina; Kartsev, Victor; Zubenko, Alexsander; Divaeva, Liudmila; Chekrisheva, Victoria; Petrou, Anthi; Oopkaew, Lipika; Somngam, Phitchakorn; Choowongkomon, Kiattawee; Rungrotmongkol, Thanyada
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子抑制剂与JAK2激酶的对接和分子动力学模拟，对象为蛋白-小分子互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Janus kinase 2 (JAK2), one of the JAK isoforms participating in a JAK/STAT signaling cascade, has been considered a potential clinical target owing to its critical role in physiological processes involved in cell growth, survival, development, and differentiation of various cell types, especially immune and hematopoietic cells. Substantial studies have proven that the inhibition of this target could disrupt the JAK/STAT pathway and provide therapeutic outcomes for cancer, immune disorders, inflammation, and COVID-19. Herein, we performed docking-based virtual screening of 63 in-house furopyridine-based compounds and verified the first-round screened compounds by in vitro enzyme- and cell-based assays. By shedding light on the integration of both in silico and in vitro methods, we could elucidate two promising compounds. PD19 showed cytotoxic effects on human erythroblast cell lines (TF-1 and HEL) with IC(50) values of 57.27 and 27.28 muM, respectively, while PD12 exhibited a cytotoxic effect on TF-1 with an IC(50) value of 83.47 muM by suppressing JAK2/STAT5 autophosphorylation. In addition, all screened compounds were predicted to meet drug-like criteria based on Lipinski's rule of five, and none of the extreme toxicity features were found. Molecular dynamic simulations revealed that PD12 and PD19 could form stable complexes with JAK2 in an aqueous environment, and the van der Waals interactions were the main force driving the complex formation. Besides, all compounds sufficiently interacted with surrounding amino acids in all crucial regions, including glycine, catalytic, and activation loops. Altogether, PD12 and PD19 identified here could potentially be developed as novel therapeutic inhibitors disrupting the JAK/STAT pathway.
abstract_zh: Janus激酶2（JAK2）作为参与JAK/STAT信号级联反应的JAK亚型之一，因其在细胞生长、存活、发育及多种细胞类型（尤其是免疫细胞和造血细胞）分化等生理过程中的关键作用，已被视为潜在的临床靶点。大量研究表明，抑制该靶点可阻断JAK/STAT通路，并为癌症、免疫紊乱、炎症及COVID-19提供治疗成效。在此，我们对63种内部呋喃并吡啶类化合物进行了基于对接的虚拟筛选，并通过体外酶学及细胞学实验验证了首轮筛选出的化合物。通过整合计算机模拟与体外方法，我们阐明了两种有前景的化合物。PD19对人红系母细胞系（TF-1和HEL）表现出细胞毒性效应，其IC(50)值分别为57.27和27.28 μM，而PD12通过抑制JAK2/STAT5自磷酸化，对TF-1表现出细胞毒性效应，IC(50)值为83.47 μM。此外，所有筛选出的化合物均被预测符合基于Lipinski五规则类药性标准，且未发现极端毒性特征。分子动力学模拟显示，PD12和PD19在水环境中能与JAK2形成稳定复合物，其中范德华相互作用是驱动复合物形成的主要力量。另外，所有化合物均能与所有关键区域（包括甘氨酸环、催化环和激活环）中的周围氨基酸充分相互作用。总之，本文鉴定的PD12和PD19有望开发为破坏JAK/STAT通路的新型治疗性抑制剂。
